caption: A glowing red-hot metal ball is set on top of a large block of ice, and the ice melts around it.

sa.check: A glowing metal ball is set on top of the block.
The ice melts around the ball.
The ball glows red at the start.
Steam or mist shows at the contact.
The ball is placed first and the melting follows.

pc.expect: The hollow under the ball only deepens and the ball settles into it; meltwater gathers there and the ice does not close back over.
pc.fail: The hollow fills back in; or the ball rises out of it with nothing lifting it; or the meltwater freezes around the glowing ball; or the ice surface returns to smooth and dry.

pc.expect: Away from the contact the ice stays a hard solid and may crack sharply; at the contact it turns to water; the ball keeps its round rigid shape.
pc.fail: The block sags or bends like wax; or the ice flows as a soft lump; or the ball squashes or spreads; or the whole block turns to slush at once while the ball touches one spot.

pc.expect: The ball's glow only fades while it sits in the ice.
pc.fail: The ball's glow brightens as it melts in; or it goes dark and glows again; or the glow spreads out into the ice around it.

pc.expect: The ball settles downward into the ice, meltwater runs down the block's sides and pools below, and any steam rises.
pc.fail: The ball climbs the block or hangs above its hollow; or meltwater runs up the block's side; or the steam sinks and pools on the ground.

pc.expect: One ball and one block; the block only loses matter and the ball stays whole.
pc.fail: The ball vanishes; or a second ball appears; or the block grows; or the ball passes out through the block's base leaving it whole above; or water appears on the block far from the ball with no melt running there.

pc.expect: The ice's look away from the contact and the surface under the block stay the same.
pc.fail: The ice turns a colour; or the ground under the block changes texture away from the water; or the block's frosted look changes all over at once.

note: The ball may sink out of sight into the block; it is then judged by the hollow and the meltwater.
